stem: Redcliff Media's finance team wants next month's NAT-related spend to go down without weakening the Availability Zone isolation Redcliff already committed to for its three-Availability-Zone private subnets. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Remove two of the three NAT gateways and route all subnets through the one that remains
Replace all three NAT gateways with a single NAT instance sized for peak traffic
Create a gateway endpoint for the Amazon S3 traffic driving most of the NAT data-processing charge
Confirm each Availability Zone's subnets route through the NAT gateway in that same Availability Zone
Turn off cost allocation tags on the NAT gateways to lower the monthly bill

rationale: A gateway endpoint removes the S3 traffic from the NAT gateway's per-GB charge entirely without touching the per-Availability-Zone topology. Confirming Availability-Zone-local routing keeps the isolation Redcliff committed to and avoids any accidental cross-Availability-Zone processing charge. Removing gateways or replacing them all with one instance both collapse the deployment back to a single point of failure. Turning off cost allocation tags has no effect on the underlying resource cost.
